x: Speechley, for one, enjoyed himself immensely Notoriously a hungry individual, he seriously contemplated going round again for another helping.
I have just received a letter from our old friend Speechley It is recalled that he sailed in November for the United States to seek fame and fortune.
I am asked to put in my notes that Charles Cook does not want to buy a dog. Several members have received letters from our old friend Speechley. He is going along merrily but misses his walk.

Speechley was noticed by his frantic efforts to catch the eyes of the attendants, as he wanted a drink. Arriving amongst the leaders we found that Rickards had now got level with Green and both were walking well.
Our "B" team—Messrs Khlopin, Dodkin, Field, (A H ) and Speechley—were placed sixth in the team handicap Khlopin was seventh in the individual handicap
Speechley (second in the indvidual handicap), S.
I remember Speechley praising the refreshments, and when he is satisfied, nothing more need be said. I did hear that he wanted to do another lap to get some more of the Derby good cheer.
Speechley, both of whom were expected to be well up.

Joe Coleman started off splendidly and although he slackened off a little in the second half of the race, he did well to take the handicap prize. Our team, consisting of Coleman, Jackman, Speechley and C.

In the second lap, however, Brown tired and eventually lost second place to Charlie Speechley, whilst Harry Churcher went on to win by about 270 yards in the exceptionally fast time of 56 min. 53 sec.—the fastest yet recorded over the course by any walker qualified to take part in the R.W.A.
Field, Harley, Speechley and Elson. A peculiarity of the handicap was that four men dead-heated for third place in the handicap, two of them, Field and Harley, coming from our own Club.
Half-a-mile later Brown allowed the leaders to get away and so positions remained until the half-way mark. Shortly after this Field suffered disqualificaton and Saunders and Speechley passed Harley.

Speechley was our eighth man to finish, 55th, doing his best 20 miles yet, and his position gave us the "Nijmegen Shield." Of our others to compete, Snell was unlucky to be a few seconds outside second-class standard, and Chandler should have gained valuable experience.
From the start Charlie Speechley led from R. Martin, and this was still the position at the end.

From the start Brown, Speechley, Martin, Bentley, Harley and Bentley led in a bunch, gradually spreading out as the race progressed. Brown showed his usual good form in winning, and Speechley maintained the improvement he has shown this season.

Elson, Harley, Dodkin, Snell, Chandler, Dodkin, Boddington, Willis, Speechley, Holman, Rathbone, and others are training and from these men it should be possible to find eight to retain the "Nijmegen" Shield, and four to regain the National Championship.

At this point (8 miles) Martin was 6th, Elson 13th, Churcher 27th, and Speechley 36th. From this point onwards, our first three men picked up places, but Charlie Speechley dropped right back, eventually finishing 74th.
Churcher (4), Speechley (5), C.

Speechley, Charlie Churcher, Storey, Redgrave, Reg Elson, Salter, Jones, Thorn, Dodkin, Brian, Boddington, Heather, Rutland, and all the others who may be called upon all know the value of a careful, studied, steady preparation and we may be sure of a team of determined, fit, walkers to do justice t…

Speechley again showed that he is faster than ever, and Charlie Churcher and Redgrave also distinguished themselves. In fact, the performances of the three last-named, all "Juniors," were very encouraging, as were those of Rutland, already mentioned, and Storey.

Charlie Speechley, the holder, was favourite, and went to the front from the start, closely followed by Charlie Churcher. It seemed, at the half-distance, that we were to be robbed of the close race which had been promised between these twain, for Speechley had opened up what appeared to be a winnin…

Despite early setbacks in the shape of the disqualification of Charlie Churcher and Charlie Speechley, who had both been expected to be with the leaders, and later that of Wright, who was shown to be in the wrong, as previously mentioned, our remaining “A” team men stuck gamely to their task and had…

Speechley was 10th and Bidgood 18th (both walking in Polytechnic colours); whilst Rutland and Wright finished together in 20th position. The last-named two and Treacher walked as members of Cadogan A.C.

From the start Jack Field cut out the pace, opening up a distance of 50 yards in the first mile from Bentley, Bidgood, Harley, Martin, Speechley and Rickards, all of whom appeared unconcerned at the pace set by the leader.

In the next event, the 2 Miles, we were represented by Speechley and Harley, whilst Surrey W.C. had Fisher and Burgess, the Kent champion. From the start Stone (Poly.) led, followed by the Surrey pair, and our two.
A terrific struggle was expected between the holder, C. Speechley and our Captain, C.

Once again we have a likely lot of "Juniors" and from their numbers it should be possible to find a team capable of winning once again if only they will train steadily and regularly, and not spasmodically. Names that come to the mind are Speechley, Sutton, Storey, R.
The race was slightly marred by the absence of Bridger, Elliott and Speechley, whose presence would most certainly have made the race keener.
